resources.string: How a sebaceous gland makes sebum
Sebum production
Illustration of a normal hair-associated sebaceous gland. The stages are sped up, the drawing is not to scale, and particle counts do not represent measurements.
A gland beside the hair follicle
Lobules of a hair-associated sebaceous gland sit beside the follicle in the dermis. A short duct connects the gland with the follicular canal.
New cells form at the edge
Small basal cells along the edge divide and replace the cells that mature inward. The cutaway follows one example cell.
Maturing cells accumulate lipids
As sebocytes mature toward the inside of the lobule, lipid droplets accumulate and occupy more of the cell.
The mature cell releases its contents
Near the duct, the mature cell breaks down. Its lipids and other cell contents contribute to sebum. This is called holocrine secretion.
Sebum reaches the skin surface
The sebum passes through the short duct into the follicular canal and reaches the skin surface alongside the hair shaft.
